# Testament of Reuben — 1
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** A copy of the words of Reuben, even the things which he charged his sons before he died, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life. **2** Two years after the death of Joseph his brother, when Reuben fell sick, his sons and his sons' sons gathered together to visit him. **3** And he said to them: My children, behold I am dying, and I go the way of my fathers. **4** And seeing there Judah, and Gad, and Levi, and all his brethren assembled, he said to them: Give heed, my brethren, and hear Reuben your father, the things which I command you. **5** And behold I call the God of heaven to witness against you this day, that ye walk not in the sins of youth and in fornication, wherein I was poured out, and defiled the bed of my father Jacob. **6** And I tell you that he smote me with a sore plague in my loins for seven months. **7** And had not my father Jacob prayed for me unto the Lord, the Lord would have destroyed me. **8** For I was thirty years old when I wrought the evil thing before the Lord, and for seven months I was sick unto death. **9** And after this I repented with set purpose of my soul for seven years before the Lord. **10** And wine and strong drink I drank not, and flesh entered not into my mouth, and I ate no pleasant food; but I was mourning over my sin, for it was great; such had not been done in Israel. **11** And now hear me, my children, what things I saw concerning the seven spirits of deceit, when I repented.

**2** Seven spirits therefore are appointed against man, and they are the leaders of the works of youth. **2** And the seven spirits of error are given against man from Beliar: **3** First, the spirit of fornication is seated in the nature and the senses; **4** the second, the spirit of insatiability, in the belly; **5** the third, the spirit of fighting, in the liver and gall. **6** The fourth is the spirit of obsequiousness and chicanery, that through over-eagerness he may appear comely. **7** The fifth is the spirit of pride, that one may be boastful and arrogant. **8** The sixth is the spirit of lying in destruction and jealousy, to practise deceits, and to conceal from kindred and friends. **9** The seventh is the spirit of injustice, with which are theft and acts of rapacity, that a man may fulfil the desire of his heart; for injustice works together with the other spirits by the taking of gifts.

**3** And therefore was Watchers also seized therewith; seeing that they desired of the daughters of men, they fell from heaven. **2** And these shall trouble the sons of the righteous for ever. **3** For bodies are set against men by Beliar, through fornication: and I know that the sons of Israel shall sin against the Levites, and shall war against their kingdom. **4** For fornication is the mother of all evils, separating from God, and bringing near to Beliar. **5** For I saw it inscribed in the writing of Enoch that your sons shall be corrupted in fornication, and shall do harm to the sons of Levi with the sword. **6** But they shall not be able to withstand Levi; for he shall wage the war of the Lord, and shall conquer all your hosts. **7** They shall be few in number, divided in Levi and Judah, and there shall be none of you for sovereignty, even as also our father prophesied in his blessings.

**4** Pay no heed to the face of a woman, neither associate with another man's wife, nor meddle with affairs of womankind. **2** For had I not seen Bathsheba bathing in a place under cover I had not fallen into this great iniquity. **3** For my mind taking in the thought of the woman's nakedness, suffered me not to sleep until I had wrought the abominable thing. **4** For while Jacob our father had gone to Isaac his father, when we were in Eder, near to Ephrath in Bethlehem, Bilhah became drunk and was asleep uncovered in her chamber. **5** Having therefore gone in and beheld her nakedness, I wrought the impiety without her perceiving it, and leaving her sleeping I departed. **6** And forthwith an angel of God revealed to my father concerning my impiety, and he came and mourned over me, and touched her no more.

**5** Pay heed therefore to the commandments of the Lord, my children, and be not led astray by the beauty of women; for mighty is the harm they bring upon kings. **2** For often has the appearance of women overcome mighty men, and brought them to contempt, and their kingdom to nought. **3** For a woman overcame Samson, and she delivered him up to his enemies. And she deceived Reuben in Timnath; and she brought about the captivity of Solomon and the destruction of many cities. **4** Joseph kept himself from a woman, and became a blessing. **5** Know therefore, my children, that women are evil; and since they have no power or strength over man, they use wiles by outward attractions, that they may draw him to themselves. **6** And whom they cannot bewitch by outward attractions, him they overcome by craft. **7** Moreover, concerning them, the angel of the Lord told me, and taught me, that women are overcome by the spirit of fornication more than men, and in their heart they plot against men; and by means of their adornment they deceive first their minds, and by the glance of the eye instil the poison, and then through the accomplished act they take them captive.

**6** For a woman cannot force a man openly, but only by a harlot's bearing she beguiles him. **2** Flee, therefore, fornication, my children, and command your wives and your daughters, that they adorn not their heads and faces to deceive the mind; because every woman who useth these wiles hath been reserved for eternal punishment. **3** For thus they allured the Watchers who were before the flood; for as these continually beheld them, they lusted after them, and they conceived the act in their mind; for they changed themselves into the shape of men, and appeared to them when they were with their husbands. **4** And the women lusting in their minds after their forms, gave birth to giants, for the Watchers appeared to them as reaching even unto heaven. **5** Beware, therefore, of fornication; and if you wish to be pure in mind, guard your senses from every woman. **6** And bid the women likewise not to associate with men, that they also may be pure in mind. **7** For constant meetings, even though the ungodly deed be not wrought, are to them an irremediable disease, and to us a destruction of Beliar, and an eternal reproach.

**7** For in fornication there is neither understanding nor godliness, and all jealousy dwelleth therein, and it separateth from God. **2** For these things I charge you, my children, and I will have you give ear to Reuben your father. **3** Give not heed to the beauty of women, neither set your mind on their affairs; but walk in singleness of heart in the fear of the Lord, and expend labour on good works, and on study and on your flocks, until the Lord give you a wife, whom he will, that ye suffer not as I suffered. **4** Until my father's death I had not boldness to look in his face, or to speak to any of my brethren, because of the reproach. **5** Even until now my conscience causeth me pain by reason of my impiety. **6** And yet my father comforted me; for he prayed for me unto the Lord, that the anger of the Lord might pass from me, even as the Lord shewed. **7** And thenceforth until now I have been on my guard and sinned not. **8** Therefore, my children, I say unto you, observe all things whatsoever I command you, and ye shall not sin. **9** For a pit unto the soul is the sin of fornication, separating it from God, and bringing it near to idols, because it deceiveth the mind and understanding, and leadeth young men into Hades before their time. **10** For many hath fornication destroyed; because, though a man be old or noble, it maketh him a reproach and a laughingstock with Beliar and the sons of men.

---
*End of Testament of Reuben*
